Subject: Post-demo: Model fit & ops checklist for clinical-notes extraction

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciated the deep dive into the clinical notes ingestion and how you surface medication/event timelines. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the recommended evaluation slate, immediate risks we flagged, and concrete next steps so we can get a short pilot running next week.

Quick summary (shortlist + why):
- Redwood-1.3B-Quant (q4f16): best cost/latency balance for your medium-length notes (avg tokens ~420). Verified p50=18ms/token, p95=46ms/token on A100-40GB profiles for 512-token requests. Good baseline for low-cost inference and prefix caching.
- Llama-3-13B-q4 (fp16->q4): higher ROUGE/QA recall on entity extraction in our tests (esp. medication resolution) but ~2.6x higher token cost and p95 latency ~120ms on same hardware.
- Mistral-Inference-7B (int8 experimental): strong on hallucination resistance in our clinical prompts, p99 tail is volatile for longer sequences — flagged for regression monitoring only.

Benchmarks we ran (links below):
- End-to-end throughput (TPS) with 8-concurrency load: Redwood-1.3B-Quant: 235 TPS sustained; Llama-3-13B-q4: 88 TPS sustained.
- Latency percentiles for 512-token inference (A100-40GB): p50/p95/p99 — Redwood-1.3B-Quant: 18/46/93 ms/token; Llama-3-13B-q4: 37/120/280 ms/token.

Primary risks we noted from today's sample dataset:
- Prompt sensitivity: a small subset of notes with nested bullet lists caused entity boundary errors — we'll include targeted prompts to cover those cases in the prompt-set-v2.
- Regression surface: Llama-3-13B-q4 improves recall but introduces occasional hallucinated dates (rare ~0.8% on our eval). We'll gate Llama-3-13B behind a quality regression test on your golden prompt set.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) You: share anonymized pilot subset (2000 notes) → upload link or SFTP by EOD Thu (12/10).
2) Us: we’ll provision a short Dedicated pilot pool (2x A100-40GB) and run the verification benchmarks + regression tests (3 business days). Deliverables: benchmark pack, latency traces, and a recommended rollout config. Attached: pilot-matrix.xlsx and prompt-set-v2.jsonl (starter).
3) Joint: schedule 30-min pilot kickoff to confirm SLAs and canary rules — proposed slot: Mon 12/13 10:00 PT.

If you want a quick cost sketch: baseline (production, 99% uptime, Redwood-1.3B-Quant pinned) ~= $4.2k/month for the committed capacity we sketched. Llama-3-13B increases infra spend ~2.6x.

Links: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/cobalt-2026-12 (live pack)

Thanks — I’ll start the verification run as soon as we get the sample.

Best,
Priyom

Alex — quick answers inline.

1) Latency units: the table I shared is ms per token on the A100 profile (we run tokenized p50/p95/p99). For an approximate end-to-end request, multiply by average generated tokens. For your ~600-token combined (prompt+response) use-case, Redwood-1.3B-Quant end-to-end p95 ~= 46ms/token * 600 tokens ≈ 27.6s — that’s obviously too high because we used tokenized micro-benchmarks for kernel-level comparisons. Practically we measure request-level p95 (with batching and prefix cache) — on the Dedicated pilot config we estimate request-level p95 for 600-token flows at ~600–900ms for Redwood-1.3B-Quant (with optimized batching) and ~1.8–2.4s for Llama-3-13B-q4. I’ll include a request-level trace in the verification pack.

2) Regression gating: yes — we can run a quality regression on your golden prompt set (we’ll compute F1/ROUGE and a small heuristic confidence score for hallucination risk). If a model rollout fails the thresholds we’ll automatically fall back to the pinned lower-capacity model (Redwood-1.3B-Quant) for that route. Fallback is configurable per-route and can be immediate or delayed (canary windows). We also provide an alert and a roll-back playbook in the Console.

I’ll kick off the verification bench as soon as the sample shows up. Expect the deliverable pack (benchmarks + traces + recommended rollout config) within 72 business hours of sample receipt.

—Priyom
